title: Bidder-Specific Synergies and the Evolution of Acquirer Returns
eligible_reason: No binary treatment switching on at unit-specific dates exists in any regression. The paper studies the time trend in acquirer announcement returns in a repeated cross-section of M&A deals (1980-2017). Table 3 / Figures 1-2 (Code/3_Table_3_Figures_1_2.do lines 39-87) regress acquirer CAR[-3,+3] (acar) or the estimated bidder fixed effect (a_fe_type) on announcement-year dummies y1990-y2017 (1980s as benchmark) with no FE, industry FE (a_sic2), or bidder FE (a_firm), plus deal-level controls; Table 4 (4_Table_4.do) replaces year dummies with a linear year trend (yr_trend); Tables 6-8 (7_Table_6.do, 10_Table_8.do, 8_Table_7.do) regress acar or target CAR on continuous 'bidder uniqueness' measures (uniqueness_ret, uniqueness_salesq, uniqueness_roaq, uniqueness_text) with year and industry or bidder FE; Table 9 regresses a_fe_type on uniqueness; Tables 10-11 regress uniqueness or combined/target CARs on yr_trend. Figures 5-6 (14_Figures_5_6.do) regress intangible-capital shares on year dummies for bidders vs non-bidders. Every right-hand-side variable of interest is a calendar-year dummy, a year trend, or a continuous uniqueness score; none is a unit-level adoption indicator. The only 'staggered' reference is to staggered-board data used in the Internet Appendix (README footnote 1), which does not appear in the shipped code.
design_notes: Repeated cross-section of U.S. acquirer deals from SDC Platinum (1980-2017) merged with CRSP, Compustat, Hoberg-Phillips text similarity and Peters-Taylor intangibles. Unit = deal; identifiers a_firm (acquirer CUSIP), a_sic2 (acquirer 2-digit SIC), yr (announcement year). Main estimations are reghdfe with vce(cluster a_sic2 yr). Controls (global X_control): public_stock public_cash private_cash private_stock sub_cash samesic2 crossborder hostile tender a_size a_runup_f0_bhar a_sigma_f0_ar a_q a_comp_td_a a_comp_cash_a. a_fe_type is the saved bidder fixed effect from the Table 3 col 4 regression (savefe). Event-study language in the code refers to stock-return event windows (CARs), not to a staggered-adoption event study.

specs.exclusion_reason: regressors are calendar-year dummies (secular time trend), not a unit-level binary adoption indicator; deal-level time-varying controls in cols 2-4
specs.unit_var: deal (a_firm = acquirer CUSIP for bidder FE)
specs.notes: Figure 2 (lines 74-87) repeats with a_fe_type as outcome.

specs.exclusion_reason: continuous regressor (bidder uniqueness score), not a binary adoption treatment; cross-sectional deal data
specs.sample_condition: full sample (Table 8 col 'base' uses s==1 estimation-sample flag)

data_files_note: Mock Data/ folder ships eight Stata .dta files (ms_m&a_trend25.dta 221 MB, ms_acomp.dta 69 MB, ms_pt_intangibles.dta, ms_qfund_rdq.dta, ms_crsp_name.dta, ms_link_comp_crsp.dta, ms_a_gvkey.dta, ms_t_gvkey.dta). README section D: 'All variables have been randomized and all identifiers and dates are made up ... it will not reproduce the results in the paper.' Logs/ holds Stata logs from the real (SDC, CRSP, Compustat, licensed) data.
software_note: Stata, reghdfe 5.2.9, estout/eststo, coefplot; 15 numbered do-files run by 00_run_all.do.
screener_notes: Not a staggered-adoption DiD. Year-dummy time-trend regressions and continuous-regressor cross-sectional regressions on M&A deals; mock data only. Exclude.
